question: For H(z)=(z+2)/(z+1), which transport preserves a finite projective group representation and its observer: left multiplication H*rho(g), or conjugation H*rho(g)*H^-1 with transported probes and values?

objects.groups: PSL(2,F_p) as normalized projective 2x2 matrices with nonzero square determinant
objects.action: [[a,b],[c,d]] sends z to (az+b)/(cz+d), with projective infinity cases
objects.composition: matrix product and function composition are both left-after-right

types.observer: ordered images of a declared tuple of distinct projective points

quantifiers: all normalized projective matrices in PSL(2,F_5) and PSL(2,F_7)
all ordered group-element pairs for representation and conjugation laws
all projective points for action and observer covariance
all coordinate subsets up to the first separating cardinality
all affine inputs when testing the deleted-pole control
candidate_grammar: transport a probe x to H(x) and its observed value y to H(y)
delete infinity and the pole from the affine chart
acceptance: the projective action is faithful and preserves every product
conjugation preserves identity, products, carrier membership and observer covariance
left multiplication is refused if it fails identity, codomain or product laws
affine deletion cannot return a total projective closure
the F_7 reuse passes without changing the method
work_unit: one candidate matrix, group pair, point action, observer key insertion, coordinate subset, control, or assertion; inner field/matrix dimension is at most 2 and point count at most 8
protected_boundaries: exact modular arithmetic only; no floating-point acceptance
the affine pole is never silently dropped from projective coverage
left multiplication is not renamed as conjugation or basis change
no native Adva identity, D*, free, Seal, simple-group universality or Riemann-hypothesis claim
coverage failure returns UnknownCoverage rather than closure
residual: external finite calibration over two fields; no general untrusted receipt validator, native checked-diagram binding, proof-assistant theorem, or practical-user acceptance
